t: #2500 Delete Greatest Value in Each Row
o: Each round removes the maximum of every row and adds the round-max to the answer. After sorting each row ascending, round i removes the i-th largest of each row, so the contribution of round i is the column-wise maximum of the sorted matrix at column n−1−i. Example 1: sorted rows [1,2,4],[1,3,3]; column maxes 4,3,1 → 8. Tiny constraints (50×50) make anything work; sorting is cleanest.
k: Sorting rows makes each round correspond to one column of the sorted matrix.
Answer = Σ over columns of the column maximum.
Equivalent to m heap pops per round, but sorting is simpler.

a.n: Approach 1: Sort rows, take column maxima
a.i: Sort each row ascending; for each column index, the deleted values across rows form a column; add its max to the answer.
s: For each column j from 0..n−1, add max over rows of grid[row][j] to the answer.
a.t: O(m·n log n) — sorting each of m rows of length n.

a.n: Approach 2: Heaps simulating the process literally
a.i: Give each row a max-heap; each round pop one element per row, take the round max. Direct translation of the statement — useful if asked to avoid mutating/sorting the matrix.
s: Build m max-heaps from the rows.
Repeat n times: pop from every heap, add the maximum popped value to the answer.
a.t: O(m·n log n) — heap construction dominates; pops are O(log n) each.

w: The sort-and-column-max approach is the interview favorite — one line in Python. Pitfalls: none serious; watch JavaScript's default lexicographic sort (need numeric comparator). Follow-up: what if rows had different lengths, or you needed the sequence of added values?
